definition: mean_t B_t over the reading window
direction: higher = more predicted response on average; independent of stimulus length

definition: eq. 8, trapezoidal integral of B over time (dt = 1 s)
direction: higher = more predicted response mass; grows with duration, so condition contrasts are also shown with duration and word count as covariates (F1)

definition: max_t of B after a centred 3-s moving average
direction: higher = a stronger maximum predicted response
larger = the maximum comes later in the text; depends on where the dense content sits

definition: share of seconds with B above the stimulus's median over all its keys and seconds (ASSUMED baseline)
direction: higher = the region spends more of the window above the stimulus-wide median

definition: variance across parcels of the window-mean pattern
direction: higher = a more uneven spatial pattern

definition: eq. 9, normalised entropy of the positive part of the window-mean parcel pattern
direction: 1 = predicted response spread evenly over parcels, lower = concentrated in few

definition: mean pairwise Pearson correlation of the 7 network time courses
direction: higher = networks co-fluctuate more over the reading window

definition: eq. 14, 1 - corr of window-mean parcel patterns
direction: larger = two units' predicted patterns differ more

definition: eq. 34, mean between-concept minus mean within-concept RDM distance
direction: higher = units of the same concept look more alike than units of different concepts

definition: eq. 28, AUC standardised per parcel over the 90 stimuli, winsorised at the global 1st/99th percentiles
direction: the input to plasticity eq. 29-33: which parcels a stimulus drives more than the corpus average
